title: Westville's Prison Began as a State Mental Hospital: Beatty Memorial Hospital

sources.what: Beatty Memorial Hospital, a state-run mental health facility, opened in February 1951; named for Dr. Norman Beatty; a 1974 lawsuit in U.S. District Court over prison overcrowding; Gov. Otis Bowen and the legislature transferred it to the Department of Correction; Westville Correctional Facility opened July 1979; 220-bed Maximum Control Complex added 1991
sources.who: Indiana Department of Administration, Westville Correctional Facility site history

sources.what: 'Beatty Memorial Hospital, a state run mental health facility, opened its doors to 135 mentally disabled Hoosiers in February of 1951. In 1974, a lawsuit filed by Indiana prisoners in US District Court forced the state to reduce overcrowding in its prisons'
sources.who: Indiana Department of Correction, Westville Correctional Facility facts and figures brochure

sources.what: first opened in 1951 as Beatty Memorial Hospital; converted to a correctional facility in 1979; the facility is at the end of its useful life; the new correctional facility at Westville
sources.who: Indiana Department of Correction, Westville State Prison project page

sources.what: civil division admitting patients from 17 northern Indiana counties in 1951; Maximum Security Division opened 1954, replacing the old Hospital for Insane Criminals at the Indiana State Prison, serving the criminally insane from the entire state; converted in 1979; 18,799 patients admitted 1951-1979
sources.who: Indiana Archives and Records Administration, other Indiana hospitals for the mentally ill

sources.what: the same history of Beatty (17 counties, 1954 Maximum Security Division replacing the Hospital for Insane Criminals at the Indiana State Prison)
sources.who: Indiana Historical Society, Connections (state facilities for family historians)

sources.what: 'Beatty Memorial Hospital began admitting patients in 1951 in Westville. In 1954, the maximum security division opened and replaced the old Hospital for Insane Criminals at the Indiana State Prison in Michigan City. In 1979, the hospital was converted into the Westville Correctional Center.'

the Indiana Hospital for Insane Criminals at the Michigan City prison (by 1912) held the criminally insane from across the state; its inmates were transferred to Beatty's Maximum Security Division, which became Westville Correctional Center in 1979; the new $1.2 billion prison in Westville set to open in 2027
sources.who: The Indiana Lawyer, 'New $1.2 billion state prison seeks to address recidivism'

sources.what: the inmates were transferred in 1954 to the newly opened Maximum Security Division at Westville; a school, bowling alley, beauty shop and solarium at Beatty
sources.who: Asylum Projects (Hospital for Insane Criminals; Norman Beatty Mental Hospital)

sources.what: 'Contained within the facility was an accredited school, bowling alley, beauty and barber shop, power plant, sewage disposal plant, fire department and security force'

12 of the existing buildings, mainly on the south edge of the site, removed since September 2023; 1.4 million square feet, $1.2 billion, 2027 completion; 'Originally built in 1951 as the Dr. Norman M. Beatty Memorial Hospital'
legislation passed in 1977; patients stayed until the summer of 1979; a 1974 lawsuit by Indiana prisoners over overcrowding
sources.who: Indiana Department of Correction, Westville PREA audit report (2019)

sources.what: 'In 1977, the Department of Correction obtained' the hospital
sources.who: Indiana Department of Correction, history book

sources.what: set to open in mid-2027; unused parts of the old prison will ultimately be torn down (citing IDOC)
the new prison sits directly south of the existing campus
the Michigan City hospital for insane criminals: a three story brick building, bars on windows
sources.who: Indiana Historical Society, Indiana State Prison photograph album
U.S. Court of Appeals, 7th Circuit (1989), via Leagle
Monon Railroad Historical-Technical Society, Bygone Monon: Westville

beats.text: Westville's prison began as a mental hospital.
beats.label: WESTVILLE, INDIANA
beats.credit: History: Indiana Dept. of Correction; Indiana State Archives

beats.text: Beatty Memorial Hospital opened in February 1951, for patients from 17 counties in northern Indiana.
beats.label: FEBRUARY 1951
beats.credit: Indiana Dept. of Administration; Indiana Historical Society

beats.text: In 1954, a maximum security division opened for patients the state called criminally insane, from all over Indiana.
The first ones were moved from the old Hospital for Insane Criminals at the state prison in Michigan City.
beats.label: MICHIGAN CITY
beats.credit: Indiana State Archives; The Indiana Lawyer; Indiana Historical Society

beats.text: Then prisoners sued over crowded prisons. In 1977, lawmakers voted to turn the hospital into a prison.
beats.label: 1974 TO 1977
beats.credit: Indiana Dept. of Correction; Indiana Dept. of Administration

beats.text: The last patients left in the summer of 1979. It became the Westville Correctional Center.
beats.label: SUMMER 1979
beats.credit: Indiana State Archives; Indiana Dept. of Correction; Indiana Dept. of Administration

beats.text: Now a new prison is going up next door, due in 2027, and parts of the old campus are set to come down.
beats.label: TODAY
beats.credit: ABC57 (2026); The Indiana Lawyer; Elevatus Architecture

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

end_card.pill: An active prison: view it from the road

factcheck.result: lines 1-3 supported; line 4 narrowed to 'the first ones' (courts later committed patients straight to Beatty); bowling-alley line dropped (only Wikipedia and Asylum Projects); 1977 handover and 'Westville Correctional Center' (its 1979 name) added; demolition-now line replaced with the new prison 'nearly finished next door' and parts of the old campus 'set to come down'; Michigan City picture changed from a castle gate to a three-storey brick ward with barred windows behind a wall; barred windows and night dropped from Beatty's own maximum security picture Second check: 1977 is when the legislature voted to make it a prison (patients and inmates shared the campus until summer 1979); 'nearly finished' became 'going up next door, due in 2027'.
